packages.label: הֲלָכוֹת וְתוֹדָה
packages.reason: This is the Torah's core conceptual family. The Rebbe equates thanksgiving (todah) with halakhot (laws), which are the delight of the World to Come. These are further equated with chesed (lovingkindness), birth/generation (holadah), the blood flow returning to order (tahaluchot hadamim), and the healing of the legs. The binding principle is: all of these are different expressions of the same spiritual reality — the restoration of proper order and flow, which constitutes the experience of closeness to God (olam haba). Abraham and David are the personality-anchors of this chesed/halakha identity.

merge_notes.reason: The moon (levana) is described as cold/lacking, which is the bechina of the lack that gets filled through halakhot/chesed. The Rebbe explicitly says: 'the filling of the lack (milui hachisaron), which is the bechina of holadah, bechina of halakhot' (line 12). The moon's coldness is a metaphor for the state BEFORE halakhot restore fullness. Same shared nature — the domain of lack/fullness that halakhot address.

packages.good_evil_mirror: The evil mirror for this package is the state of tzarah (distress) where blood floods the heart, and the klipah that prevents birth (kishui leiled). See Package 4 for the evil nodes.

packages.label: שַׁבָּת וְשִׂמְחָה
packages.reason: This package spans both the holy domain (Shabbat = son = joy = rest = simple unity) and its weekday counterpart (Metatron = servant = sadness = six weekdays). The Torah explicitly contrasts these two poles as parallel aspects: Shabbat IS the bechina of 'son' and joy, while the weekdays ARE the bechina of 'servant' and sadness. They form one thematic family because the Torah's argument is precisely about drawing the joy of Shabbat into the weekdays — transforming the servant-domain via the son-domain. Noach (rest), Chanukah (chanu-kaf-heh = rested on the 25th), leshon hakodesh (holy tongue), and achdut hapashut (simple unity) are all parallel expressions of the Shabbat quality. Chanoch/Metatron/Eved are the weekday pole.
packages.good_evil_mirror: This package contains its own internal good/evil mirror. The good pole: Shabbat, Ben (son), Simcha (joy), Noach (rest), Achdut Hapashut (simple unity), Leshon Hakodesh. The evil pole: Metatron, Eved (servant), Atzvut (sadness), weekdays, Chanoch. The point of fracture is Chanukah itself — which is both 'chanu kaf-heh' (Shabbat rest) AND 'Chanoch' (Metatron/servant/weekdays). Chanukah is where the two poles meet.

packages.label: רִבּוּעַ הַדִּבּוּר וְהָאֱמֶת
packages.label_en: The Four Parts of Speech and Truth
packages.reason: The Torah describes a four-part structure of speech (ribua hadibbur): speech of tzedakah, teshuvah, wealth, and malkhut. Each part has a parallel proof in R' Eliezer's four demonstrations (carob=tzedakah, water channel=teshuvah, walls of beit midrash=wealth, bat kol=malkhut). The three divine names (El, Elokim, Havaya) are the sources of truth that illuminate this four-part speech, and they parallel tefillah, Torah, and shidduchim respectively. The oil of Chanukah = or ha'emet (light of truth). All these are parallel aspects of the same domain: complete, truth-filled speech as the vehicle for divine revelation.

merge_notes.reason: The speech of tzedakah is explicitly one of the four parts of the ribua hadibbur. The carob tree is its bechina parallel in R' Eliezer's proofs. All are aspects of the same dibbur structure.
Bat kol is explicitly the bechina of malkhut, and this is the fourth part of the ribua hadibbur (dibbur shel malkhut = 'gam me'az dabrekha'). Part of the same four-part speech structure.
The three divine names (El Elokim Havaya) are the mekhor ha'emet — the source of truth that illuminates the ribua hadibbur. They are the structural backbone of the dibbur package.
El = tefillah = koach. This is the unpacking of the first of the three names. El is a bechina of power/prayer, which illuminates the dibbur.
Elokim = Torah = Rav. This is the unpacking of the second of the three names. Part of the same dibbur/emet family.
Oil (shemen) is the bechina of or ha'emet (light of truth), which heals the lungs and is the tikun of the tzarah. The oil is the physical embodiment of the emet that fills the dibbur.

Explicitly connected via 'anshei damim yis'nu tam' — men of blood hate the complete (tam/emet). Evil polarity within the emet domain.

merge_notes.reason: These are the central structural concept of the entire dibbur family — the square of speech = four parts of speech. The hub of this package.

merge_notes.reason: The fourth of the four parts of speech. 'Gam me'az' = malkhut peh = the speech of kingship.
The name Havaya (YHVH) is the bechina of shidduchim (matchmaking). Third of the three divine names that illuminate dibbur.
The water channel in R' Eliezer's proof is the bechina of teshuvah. Parallel to the dibbur shel teshuvah.

merge_notes.reason: The walls of the beit midrash in R' Eliezer's proof are the bechina of the wealthy. Parallel to the dibbur shel ashirut.

merge_notes.merged_component: Comp 19: שמן של נר חנוכה — אור האמת (2 nodes)
merge_notes.reason: The oil of the Chanukah candle is the bechina of or ha'emet (light of truth). This is the concrete Chanukah manifestation of the emet that illuminates dibbur.

packages.good_evil_mirror: The evil mirror within this package is the node pair 'דמים שוטפין על הלב = פגם האמת' (blood flooding the heart = damage to truth). When truth is damaged, the four-part speech cannot function — the dibbur is in exile ('lo ish devarim anokhi'). The entire package describes the RESTORATION of complete speech through truth.

packages.label: קְלִפָּה וְקִשּׁוּי לֵילֵד
packages.label_en: The Shell and Difficulty in Childbirth
packages.reason: The klipah (evil shell) that says 'Cut! Neither for me nor for you' is the bechina of difficulty in childbirth. This is a small but distinct evil domain: the force that prevents the holadah (birth/generation) from emerging into the world. It is the evil mirror of Package 1's holadah/halakhot cluster.

merge_notes.reason_kept_separate: While this is thematically the evil mirror of Package 1's holadah, it is connected by bechina language as its own independent evil domain. The klipah is not an aspect of halakhot — it is the OPPOSING force. Keeping it separate preserves the good/evil mirror structure clearly. The framework states that the same concept can appear in both a good and evil package.

packages.good_evil_mirror: This is the evil mirror of Package 1's birth/generation cluster. Package 1 describes halakhot generating new life; Package 4 describes the klipah preventing birth.
